intro: Southeast Asia is home to many martial arts with long histories. In Thailand, boxing grew from temple fairs and royal events into a ring sport with stadiums, gloves and a national law. Across the Malay world, silat is a large family of arts shown at weddings and in scored matches. In the Philippines, arnis became the national martial art by law in 2009.

These arts also traveled. Filipino farm workers taught eskrima in California backyards. Indo families brought pencak silat to the Netherlands. Thai boxing camps now welcome students from around the world, and a bundle of arnis sticks can sit in a Chicago school closet. Each move brought new rooms, new rules and new questions about names.

In this unit you will read about objects like the mongkon and the pra jiad, and about bodies like IPSI, PERSILAT, IFMA and WEKAF. You will compare legends with records. By the end, you will be able to explain how an art can live in a stadium, a village and a school gym at the same time.
bigQuestion: How do martial arts from Southeast Asia keep their meaning when they move into stadiums, federations and gyms far from home?

test.q: What does the Thai word muay mean?
test.why: Muay is the Thai word for boxing.

test.q: Which object often stays on during a Muay Thai match?
test.why: The pra jiad armband often stays on, while the mongkon comes off before the first round.

test.q: Why do many Thai teachers object to the mongkon as a costume?
choices: It marks the bond between teacher and boxer.
It is only worn by referees.
test.why: Many gyms see the mongkon as a sign of the teacher and student bond.

test.q: Which stadium opened first in Bangkok?
test.why: Rajadamnern opened in 1945, before Lumpinee in 1956.

test.q: How should the Nai Khanom Tom story be described?
choices: as a legend honored in Thailand
test.why: The story comes from later writings; it is a legend honored on National Muay Thai Day.

test.q: Which country calls its ring sport lethwei?
test.why: Lethwei is the traditional ring sport of Myanmar.

test.q: What does IOC recognition of IFMA in 2021 mean?
choices: Muay Thai was in the 2021 Games.
The IOC accepts IFMA as the sport's world body.
test.why: Recognition means the IOC accepts IFMA as the world body; it does not add the sport to a Games by itself.

test.q: Which statement about silat is correct?
choices: It began in one village in 1948.
It is only practiced in Thailand.
It is a single school with one teacher.
It is a family of arts across the Malay world.
test.why: Silat is a family of many arts practiced across the Malay world.

test.q: What is the difference between IPSI and PERSILAT?
choices: IPSI is Indonesia's national body; PERSILAT is international.
IPSI is Thai; PERSILAT is Filipino.
IPSI is a drum; PERSILAT is a dance.
test.why: IPSI (1948) is Indonesia's national body; PERSILAT (1980) is the international federation.

test.q: In sport pencak silat, what are seni events?
test.why: Seni means art; seni events are judged on set routines.

test.q: Where do the names arnis and eskrima come from?
choices: Spanish words, from more than 300 years of Spanish rule
test.why: Arnis likely comes from Spanish arnés, and eskrima from Spanish esgrima.

test.q: What did Republic Act No. 9850 do in 2009?
choices: made arnis the national martial art and sport
test.why: Republic Act No. 9850 made arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines.

test.q: Why is the claim that Lapulapu's fighters used arnis called a tradition?
choices: No record from 1521 names such an art.
It was written in the 2009 law.
It comes from a Thai chronicle.
test.why: Pigafetta's journal names weapons but no martial art, so the claim is a tradition.

test.q: Which U.S. law cut Filipino immigration to 50 people a year?
choices: the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
test.why: The Tydings-McDuffie Act of 1934 set a quota of 50 Filipino immigrants a year.

test.q: How do historians of the diaspora see an art in a gym and at a festival?
choices: Both settings are part of the art's history.
test.why: Historians see both the sport gym and the community gathering as real parts of the art's history.

write.prompt: Is an art still the same art when it moves from a village or temple fair to a stadium, a federation or a school gym? Argue your answer using two or three dates, laws or records from this unit, such as the Boxing Act of 1999, Republic Act No. 9850 or the 2019 UNESCO list.
tips: Name each date, law or record you use.
Label legends as legends, and set them beside records.
Say who holds a belief, such as many Thai gyms or many arnis teachers.
Compare two settings instead of calling one real and one fake.
Use unit words such as federation, diaspora and mongkon.
